subject: Streaming socket latency & error surge during peak - BrightCommerce
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcommerce.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCommerce SRE <sre@brightcommerce.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in streaming chat p95/p99 during peak - seeing many 504s

Hi Kimberly —

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency on the streaming chat endpoint during our weekday peak (11:45–12:30 PT). p95 has drifted from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99 is up to ~3.6s. We're also seeing intermittent 504s for open connections. This started around 11:40 PT and has persisted in waves.

Datadog link: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/abcd-1234/brightcommerce-sse-latency (screenshot attached)

Impact: several customer sessions dropped during our peak sales promo — it's customer-facing and causing revenue risk.

Can you triage and advise immediate mitigation steps? We need an ETA for resolution and any recommended mitigations we can apply on our side.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Reliability
BrightCommerce
[Attachment: dd-screenshot-tail-graphs.png (image/png)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: infra <dev.patel@redwood.com>, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcommerce.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in streaming chat p95/p99 during peak - seeing many 504s

Folks — forwarding BrightCommerce alert. They're seeing sustained p95/p99 regressions and 504s during their peak window (11:40–12:30 PT). Seen similar tail pattern across a handful of hosted API customers earlier this week.

Immediate asks:
- Confirm whether this is an infra/Kestrel-related regression or a routing/batching/backpressure issue.
- If it's capacity/queueing, can we temporarily route BrightCommerce traffic to the Dedicated fallback pool or enable the kv-prefix cache for their route?
- Collect any Kafka/Kestrel logs around 11:30–12:45 PT; attach to thread.

Looping in Marcus for serving runtime impact and Hannah/Rishi for exec briefing and credit decision. Emily — we'll keep you updated every 30 minutes.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
[Attachment: runbook-fallback.md (text/md)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcommerce.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in streaming chat p95/p99 during peak - seeing many 504s

Kim and Marcus — quick triage notes:

Observations (10:00–10:04 PT):
- We see a correlated increase in acceptance queue time on the frontend proxies servicing SSE/WebSocket routes for the hosted API.
- Kestrel CPU utilization spikes precede the latency increases by ~30s. There are bursts of GC/compaction on a subset of instances.
- Error pattern: connection timeouts (504) during long-lived connections under bursty token emission.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:03 PT):
- Enabled autoscaler bump for the affected pool (added 4x temporary workers for 15 minutes).
- Applied a soft limit to per-connection token emission (throttled tail-heavy clients) to reduce KV cache churn.

Attached diagnostic logs (snippet) and my suggested short-term routing: route BrightCommerce to Dedicated-fallback (if they approve) OR enable per-customer kv-prefix caching which should drop p99 by ~40% from our sim runs.

Attaching: diagnostic-kestrel-logs.txt

—Dev
Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: diagnostic-kestrel-logs.txt (text/plain)]

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcommerce.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCommerce SRE <sre@brightcommerce.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in streaming chat p95/p99 during peak - seeing many 504s

Thanks for the quick triage. We accepted a short-lived routing change at 10:10 PT and saw partial improvement through 10:30–11:00, but the pattern resurfaced during their higher concurrency window (11:45–12:20).

Notes from our SRE: during the 11:45 window we had a bimodal distribution of sequence lengths (many long sessions + many short sessions), which likely increased KV cache misses. Appreciate the kv-prefix cache suggestion — do you have an ETA to enable it for us? If routing to Dedicated is required, we need a timeline and any cost/contract implications.

We can provide additional traffic samples if that helps.

-Emily

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcommerce.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief — BrightCommerce streaming latency surge (need decision on Dedicated fallback + credit)

Hannah / Rishi —

Summary: BrightCommerce (key mid-market customer; high-visibility flash promo) experienced repeat p95/p99 regressions on our hosted streaming endpoint during their peak (11:40–12:30 PT). Our infra team applied autoscaler bumps and soft throttling which gave partial relief. Root cause is currently suspected to be KV-cache churn with a bimodal session-length distribution—this increases per-connection work and triggers CPU/GC spikes in Kestrel on some instances.

Options and recommended next steps:
1) Enable per-customer kv-prefix caching for BrightCommerce (low-impact, can ship in ~3 hours with current infra patch). Expected p99 reduction ~30–45%.
2) Temporarily route them to Dedicated-fallback pool for the remainder of their promo window (requires Ops approval; expected <30min cutover). Potential commercial implication: we should offer a one-off credit for customer disruption — recommend 10% of that month's usage as a gesture.
3) Post-incident: schedule a runbook change to detect bimodal session distributions and proactively enable caching for affected customers.

Supportive artifacts: diagnostic logs, Datadog screenshots, runbook.

Requesting approval to route to Dedicated-fallback now and to pre-approve the one-off credit. If approved, I'll coordinate cutover with Dev & Marcus and notify BrightCommerce.

-Kim

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightcommerce.com>
